svg.title: gov-tla A1 — How every count in the README is made: six modules, two results files each, and the build that checks the README against them
svg.desc: Each module is checked by TLC from its row list and proved by TLAPS in a proof module that extends it; each run writes a dated results file that is never edited. 2,156 TLC rows, every one as expected, and 6,965 proof obligations, every one proved, read from the twelve named files below when this diagram is built. The build fails if any README count, digest or file name disagrees. Liveness and Government.tla's global reachability claims are checked, not proved, and none of it is a claim about law or practice.

text.tspan: How every count in the README is made: six modules, two results files each, and the build that checks the README against them

g.text: Each module is checked by TLC from its row list and proved by TLAPS in a proof module that extends it; each run writes a dated results file that is never edited. 2,156 TLC rows, every one as expected, and 6,965 proof obligations, every one proved, read from the twelve named files below when this diagram is built. The build fails if any README count, digest or file name disagrees. Liveness and Government.tla's global reachability claims are
checked, not proved, and none of it is a claim about law or practice.

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. Sampled means random simulation found no error, and is never cited as a check. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked). PROOF-GAPS.txt lists no module without a proof module.

text.tspan: From a module to its evidence: two generators that write, four scripts that only read (README § Running)
Generators: write results/ only when everything is as expected

svg.text: The model. Its header names each mutation and the property it must break. Mut = "none" is the text
(README § How …, Mutations).
The only input of a TLC run: header comments give the module, title, prose expectation and default
constants; each row is one run and the verdict it must give (tlc_rows.py docstring).
Runs every row with -workers 1. Writes the dated file only if every row is as expected, never overwrites
one; a differing rerun gets a letter suffix. Refuses a TLC not in tools/TLC-PIN (README § Running, Pins).
Names the checker by sha256, every module and the row list by sha256, the constants and the
expectation, then one line per row and a summary line.
Extends the module without editing it. Proves each safety property as Spec => []P, assuming only that the
mutations which break P are absent; SafeAlways under Mut = "none"; one lemma per mutation saying
what it admits (README § How …, Proofs).
Runs tools/tlapm --cleanfp --strict with a throwaway cache. Writes the file only if every
obligation is proved. tools/tlapm refuses a prover not in tools/TLAPS-PIN (README § Running).
Names every module of the EXTENDS chain and the prover by sha256, each theorem with its hypotheses,
the lemmas, and the TLC results file that holds the mutations' counterexamples and the witnesses, by
sha256.
the proof module and its EXTENDS chain
EXTENDS, never edits
cites it by sha256

text.tspan: Audits: read the results files and the tree, never write results/

svg.text: For every module, compares each digest on the newest results files' Modules: lines with the tree, and the
checker and prover with their pins: IN SYNC, STALE or MISSING. A module with no proof module needs a
line in PROOF-GAPS.txt (docstring).
.github/workflows/checks.yml reruns row lists and proofs in the tla-kit image pinned by digest (
tools/TLA-KIT-PIN) and compares each fresh file with the newest committed one, line for line except the
date. CI never writes to results/ (README § Running, CI).
Chooses the modules a change can affect: its EXTENDS chain, row list, committed results, the scripts, the
pins or the workflow. One row list can take two hours on a 2-CPU runner; a manual run checks every
module (docstring; README § Running).
Flips one Mut # "M_X" hypothesis to Mut = "M_X" in a scratch copy and requires the proof to fail in a
statement that carries it. Writes nothing to the tree ("a mutated proof is not an artefact", docstring).

text.tspan: What every module must have (README § How the specs are written and checked)

svg.text: One action could break each property, and that action's guard decides whether it does.
Three kinds: a state predicate whose inductive step is that guard; a flag the violating step
would raise (tenDayBreach, payCut, warWithoutStatute); a record written once and
checked against the guard of the step that wrote it.
A constant Mut: "none" is the text; each other value removes exactly one check, and the
module header names the property that removal must break.
Where they exist, real earlier law. TLC must find a counterexample for every mutation against
every property it breaks, and none against any other.
Each Never… property says something the text allows never happens. TLC must find each one
violated, which shows the model reaches those states.
Without them, a property could hold only because the state it forbids is unreachable.
<Module>_proof.tla extends the module without editing it and proves each safety property
as Spec => []P, assuming only that the mutations which break P are absent.
Also SafeAlways under Mut = "none", and one lemma per mutation saying what it admits.
All of it is in results/, generated by scripts/ and never edited.
Each file is dated and names the checker or prover, and every module it covers, by sha256.

svg.text: A witness is counted as an unmutated row on a Never… property, invariant or temporal; a mutation as each Mut value other than "none" that a results file runs. With those two readings every README count matches (the diagram's definitions, not the README's, which states none).

A COUNTEREXAMPLE row is as expected when the row list expects it: a mutation's broken property or a witness. A DEADLOCK row runs with the deadlock check on: HOLDS means none was reached, DEADLOCK that one was, as its row list expects. NO-ERROR-SAMPLED is a sample and never a check (each results file's Words: line). Every row in every file is as expected; the build fails otherwise.

text.tspan: What is not proved, and why (README § How …, What is not proved)

svg.text: PresentedBillsResolve, ActingEventuallyEnds, UnconstitutionalEdgesAreStruck, MajorityPrevails, ReconciliationPrevails are checked by TLC,
not proved.
Each is a leads-to quantified over bills, agencies or edges, and the pinned prover has no sound route for a quantified leads-to.
Elections.tla's ExecutiveIsFilled has no quantifier and is proved, by one WF1 step.
Checked, not proved. They are stated over Reach, a recursive function the prover has no fixpoint theory for.
Each one's local form is proved.
Existential, and stay with TLC: a run that reaches a state is evidence that it is reachable at those constants, and no proof is attempted.

text.tspan: The flip tests: two records side by side (the diagram's juxtaposition; no results file records a flip)
README § How the specs are written and checked

svg.text: "Every flip test fails as required: with one mutation hypothesis flipped to Mut = "M_X", each proof breaks in the lemma of the property that mutation must break."
"The recorded flips ran under the script's earlier rule (a failure anywhere outside SafeAlways) … The script now requires a failure in a statement that carries the
flipped hypothesis, and the flips have not been re-run under that rule."
The assessment is of four modules, as of commit e86e3c9 (its opening).
scripts/flip_test.py writes nothing to the tree, by design, so neither statement has a results file behind it, and no file says which rule each recorded flip ran
under.
results/ holds TLC and proof results files only.

Sources: README.md § How the specs are written and checked (its bullets, the summary table, the flip-test sentence, What is not proved), § Running (the scripts, Pins, CI); scripts/tlc_rows.py, proof_results.py, proof_sync.py, compare_results.py, ci_plan.py, flip_test.py (docstrings); .github/workflows/checks.yml; docs/ASSESSMENT.md § Strengths, point 2; PROOF-GAPS.txt; results/Constitution-results-2026.11.18.txt, results/Constitution-proof-results-2026.11.18.txt; results/Judiciary-results-2026.11.09.txt, results/Judiciary-proof-results-2026.11.17.txt;
